pairs.subject: data-retention
pairs.evidence: app/data/[token]/DataClient.tsx:252 The confirmation screen tells the candidate what goes and what stays through fixed catalog copy (eraseExplainer/confirmBody), plus a 'what we hold' list built by a separate presence projection (heldDataCategories). Neither comes from the scrub that anonymizeEntry actually performs, so a table added to or kept by the erasure can drift from what the page promises without anything failing.

techniques.evidence: app/data/[token]/DataClient.tsx:134 An on-demand door for the data subject. A failed POST re-reads the authoritative state, because the token is nulled on the first scrub, so a replay or a second tab never shows 'not erased' for data that is already gone. Backend: route.ts:86 calls the same anonymizeEntry primitive that the expiry sweep (anonymizeExpiredConsents) uses, and the copy names the retained carve-outs (de-identified record, sealed decision log, hosted voice copy).

app/data/[token]/DataClient.tsx:252 What is removed and what survives are both named on the same screen as the confirmation (good). The removed and kept items are static copy, though, and the held list (line 158, heldDataCategories) is a second implementation rather than output from anonymizeEntry's scrub list. That is the parallel-implementation failure the technique names.

app/data/[token]/DataClient.tsx:318 A yes/no alertdialog gates the irreversible erase. The echo exists to catch a wrong-target error by an operator choosing among targets. Here a single-target capability token binds the target (one entry), and the actor is the data subject using their own statutory right, so there is no target to mis-pick and no distinctive name to echo.

app/data/[token]/DataClient.tsx:122 No configurable window drives this deletion. It is a live, human-initiated erase of one entry, which is exactly the technique's 'already gated on a live human' exclusion.

app/data/[token]/DataClient.tsx:245 The page only displays the horizon stamped on the row (consent_expires_at, the same column the expiry sweep's predicate reads, pipeline.ts:2940). It sets no window and resolves no default.

app/api/data/[token]/route.ts:86 The page's backend erases one entry in a single transaction. No volume purge, batch loop or runner budget is involved here; the scheduled sweep lives elsewhere (anonymizeExpiredConsents).

pairs.registryProposal: confirm-by-echo should state its precondition as 'an actor who could pick the wrong target among several'. A data subject erasing their own record through a single-target capability link has no wrong-target error to catch. Adding typed-echo friction there also cuts against the regulatory duty to make exercising erasure easy, so the technique should list self-service subject erasure under 'When not to use this'.
